summary: NASA and Katalyst Space have abandoned plans for a commercial reboost of the Swift space telescope following the failure of a private effort to save the orbital observatory. In international launch developments, Chinese firm LandSpace successfully recovered a Zhuque-3 rocket booster on land during its second orbital flight. Lunar exploration updates show NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter imaged a crater created by an impacting SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, while new agency research indicates human-related microbes may be capable of surviving at the moon's South Pole. In commercial industry news, hypersonic missile startup Castelion raised $1 billion in funding, and Firefly Aerospace agreed to fly a Zeno Power radioisotope heating unit on a future lunar lander mission. On the military front, the Congressional Budget Office reported that the Pentagon rebuffed repeated requests for briefings on the secretive Golden Dome initiative, unexplained Russian space activity reportedly forced a U.S. Air Force flight to Antarctica to turn around, and the U.S. Space Force announced it will continue operating legacy weather satellites until at least 2028 while developing replacements. Aboard the International Space Station, spacewalkers successfully removed a failed antenna but ran out of time to install its replacement. In scientific discoveries, astronomers identified the fastest known star in the Milky Way, traveling around the central supermassive black hole at 15,500 miles per second. Looking ahead, industry observers should watch for Rocket Lab to test an orbital data network connection for the U.S. Space Force in 2027.
